candidate.title: Nuc-Seq / SNES
candidate.scope: Architecture of the assigned Illumina poster middle row labeled Nuc-Seq / SNES: the G2/M single-nucleus genomic-DNA amplification component from candidate selection through the DNA endpoint. Nuc-Seq and SNES are distinct grouped targets, not aliases. The left Single cell genome icons are descriptive examples; only the middle selection/amplification arrows form the extracted route. The upper MALBAC row, its primer legend and cycling loop, and the lower LIANTI row and its RNA/UMI stages are neighboring context with no connection to this row. The row shows a retained individual and excluded candidates, not pooling or an alternative amplification arm. Primary text resolves the cell-cycle and nuclear-lysis interface captions. The scope is schematic, not a claim that both complete published implementations share every depicted treatment: the S1 step has diagram-level support only. The endpoint is amplified nuclear DNA; downstream library construction, Nuc-Seq genome/optional-exome readout, and SNES exome capture are used only to interpret what that DNA can represent and are not added as unshown operations.

The primary Nuc-Seq implementation uses downstream genome sequencing or optional exome capture; SNES uses downstream exome capture. Thus exome specificity is not conferred by phi29 amplification or the drawn S1 treatment.
Downstream DNA reads represent sequences and variants from the retained nucleus; SNES can report exonic SNVs and indels after capture. These DNA workflows do not measure RNA expression.

operations.label: phi29 / Limited amplification
operations.description: Use the accessible single-nucleus genomic DNA as the template for limited amplification, producing the first depicted DNA structure with displaced arms. Phi29 is a polymerase catalyst, not a biological template or a separate material-transfer branch.

operations.information_effect: Creates amplifiable DNA copies representing the selected nuclear genome. Limiting amplification is intended to mitigate technical errors, without guaranteeing complete genome representation.

unknowns.question: Which member-specific published implementation uses the depicted S1 nuclease treatment, and what DNA structure is its substrate? The drawing supports a branched-to-straight-DNA treatment, but the inspected Nuc-Seq full-text passages describe downstream Tn5/TA library routes and SNES Methods describe sonication/TA libraries without establishing an S1 step. A primary passage specifying S1 substrate and product for Nuc-Seq and/or SNES would be required to assign detailed chemistry to a published implementation. This does not block extraction of the shared schematic; complete-protocol equivalence and exact cleavage chemistry are withheld.

checks.rationale: The image literally combines an S-phase expansion with a G2/M sorting caption. Wang describes genome duplication during S phase and specifically gates G2/M nuclei; SNES independently permits G2/M. The correction preserves the original wording and interprets this local route as post-replication G2/M throughout s_selected, s_template and downstream operations. It does not silently add a G1/0 branch.
